correctness.rationale: Poisson marking yields the exact bivariate generating function; independent Palm differentiation yields the first-binding time/live-count joint density. Differentiation gives a finite conditional mean even when EJ squared is infinite because the singular term integrates to mu-psi_prime(q(t)). The early size-biased limit follows from uniform small-age limits; Karamata/Riemann-sum estimates produce the three regimes and Brownian erfc asymptotics fix constants. 54 forward-equation and six finite power-tail numerical comparisons passed, but are not proof of asymptotics.

value.rationale: The observable is the natural number of independently living searchers at the instant the first target reaction occurs, a useful selection-biased copy-number statistic distinct from average waiting time and unconditional abundance. The theorem identifies the exact finite-versus-divergent conditional mean boundary (finite 2nd burst moment), a critical inverse-time law, and a strong essential rare-event amplification regime. It is a structural identification and sharp natural classification rather than a fixed-parameter recomputation. Extreme-time events may be statistically hard to observe.
